items.evidence: I looked at sfx1_wicks_ab.png and sfx1_runtime_mix_ab.png, then re-captured on a fresh prod build with two seats and seeds the engineer did not use. probe_audio_runtime match --fighter lisvel --seed 3 --seconds 300: all 7 gates PASS; fighters 53.5 %, library 30.5 %, Wicks 10.5 %; c_hit_phys_light fell to 5.0 % (was 18-19 %); c_proj_whoosh is out of the top 10. --fighter odrum --seed 7: all gates PASS, fighters 63.5 %. So the claimed 50.3 % holds on other seeds and is not a lucky one. All four Wicks are bound to their own w_* cues in content/units.json (4 takes each), and the wick gate passes in audio/build.py --gates. In the engine diff, the projectile case skips the whoosh for minions and kitted fighters; Wick-on-Wick hits play at 0.32, or 0.2 when they are dense; the shooters map handles a shot that lands after its shooter died. Residual: my own time-frequency take similarity is 0.987-0.994 median across the Wick takes, which is barely more varied than the library cues they replace (c_hit_phys_light 0.984). The kit share is an engine-side sum of gain squared (__valeAudio.heard), not a measurement of the output.

Read the diff in src/audio/index.ts. A ±1.2 dB random gain goes in its own GainNode after the voice gain, only on spatial sfx one-shots with pitchVar > 0. A repeat within 120 ms plays -1.5 dB down and up to 4 ms late, and the start and retire times are offset to match. This is a real anti-machine-gun measure and the deterministic level stays readable to probes. The build half (recipe-varied takes) was attempted and reverted, and is honestly listed as not done.

sfx5_structures_ab.png: before, structures were silent when struck; after, Needle, Lantern and Hourbell each have their own struck cue (3 takes; my measured centroids are 507, 603 and 315 Hz, so they are distinct materials), and the Lantern and Hourbell have their own falls (c_lantern_fall's 1.38 s glass collapse, c_hourbell_fall's 4.07 s bell crack and landing) instead of one shared rumble. The live Odrum capture heard c_struck_needle. Bindings are 'structureStruck.<unit>' and 'structureFall.<unit>' in content/audio.json, with no content ids in src. The camp half is not done.

sfx6_zones_ab.png plus my own seam check on all 15 f_*_zone loops: the jump from the last sample to the first is at most 0.82x the file's own p99 sample step, and the RMS of the first 20 ms is within 0.6 dB of the last 20 ms, so there is no loop click. They are quiet (-22 to -33 dBFS RMS), so they sit under the fight. The as-heard gate reports 20 own area bindings, with 0 library cues under kitted zones or ults.

sfx7_states_ab.png: one sine-ladder c_buff for 4 states became 3 distinct cues (haste is an air streak with centroid 1258 Hz; unstoppable is an iron set with chain at 437 Hz, 5.5 ms rise; veil is a 1291 Hz shimmer). Shield break is a new glass crack (4.5 ms rise, 2-6 kHz 15 %). The engine reads dst.shield from the view contract (src/contracts/sim.ts:104 has shield) and e.shielded from combat.ts, so it is presentation only. The control-distinct gate passes.

sfx8_gleam_ab.png and my own measurement: m_gleam now has a 1.8 ms rise (was 38 ms), centroid 1447 Hz and 2-6 kHz at 14.7 % (was 2.3 %), so it reads as a crisp coin instead of a soft sine. There is a 2-rung ladder that steps up within 1.5 s through CueOpts.rate, and an own kill spill (m_gleam_kill, 4 coins). This is close to the satisfaction of the gauge without copying it.

sfx9_rooms_ab.png and the live captures: room.on true, rift IR 0.69 s in both of my runs. There is one shared ConvolverNode with normalize on, it returns on the sfx bus (ducks and volume apply), the send is distance-scaled from -20 dB to -11 dB, UI, announcer and music stay dry, and it is guarded on createConvolver. Each map has its own IR (rift 0.69 s, bridge 0.88 s, fray 0.60 s). This adds space the dry mix lacked. master integrated loudness stayed in tokens (masterIntegratedInTokens PASS in both captures).
Not attempted. The kit hits are still dark and soft: f_lisvel_hit is 3.1 % in 2-6 kHz and 0.0 % above 6 kHz by my FFT. This was the plan's highest-impact gap against the gauge and it is still open.
Not attempted (per-ability Q/W/E impacts). Ability hits still share one f_<fighter>_hit.
Not done. The hand-off to the UI lane (shop.tsx plays shop_buy on click) is a reasonable reason.

problems.what: SFX-2 (impact transient and air) and the build half of SFX-3 (recipe-varied takes) were not delivered. These were the plan's two biggest gaps against the gauge, so blows still thud rather than crack, and the takes of the kit hits stay near-clones.
problems.evidence: My FFT: f_lisvel_hit 2-6 kHz 3.1 %, >6 kHz 0.0 %; take TF-similarity 0.996. The engineer's notDone list agrees.
problems.fix: Next session: a crack() transient layer per fighter material, with a VOICING re-search so the 8 dB identity bar holds, then 4-5 per-take recipes for hit, attack_hit and attack_swing.

problems.what: Garbled comments in src/audio/index.ts: trailing comments for SHOOTERS_MAX and SHIELD_BREAK_GAP_S were spliced onto the STRUCK_GAP_S line, the shooters and shieldBroke field comments were spliced onto the roomOn line, and the JSDoc of kit() now sits above wickDuck(), so the wrong function carries it.
problems.evidence: git diff 75ab44c52 HEAD -- src/audio/index.ts: 'const STRUCK_GAP_S = 0.15; // … at most this often per structure // attackers remembered ... // one target's shield breaks ...'; 'private roomOn = false; // … live once ... // the last attackers ... // a target's last shield break'.
problems.fix: Move each comment to its own constant or field, and move the kit() JSDoc back above kit().

problems.what: The new Wick cues are not clearly more take-varied than the library cues they replace, by a time-frequency measure.
problems.evidence: My 1/3-octave spectrogram correlation, median across takes: w_wick_hit 0.993, w_wick_hit_heavy 0.994, w_glimwick_hit 0.994, versus c_hit_phys_light 0.984. The build gate passes only on its smoothed long-term spectrum metric (<= 0.985).
problems.fix: Vary the transient and the decay envelope per take, not only the spectrum, and add a time-frequency similarity gate.

problems.what: fighterKitShareGe50 is an engine-side proxy (sum of gain x attenuation squared per play), and it passed only narrowly on the engineer's own seed (50.27 %).
problems.evidence: probe_audio_runtime.mjs kitShare reads window.__valeAudio.heard. My runs: 53.5 % (lisvel seed 3) and 63.5 % (odrum seed 7), so it is not flaky on these seeds, but it has thin margin on a laning seat.
problems.fix: Optionally confirm with a per-bus output meter, and keep the margin when the Wick gains are retuned.

problems.what: Several A/B sheet titles overlap their subtitle (sfx1, sfx5, sfx7, sfx8, sfx9), so the header is hard to read.
problems.evidence: Read the PNGs: the title text is drawn over the right-aligned legend.
problems.fix: Wrap the title or move the legend to a second line in audio/sfx_ab.py.

problems.what: probe_audio_qpop E fails ('master 0 still plays the pop'). The engineer says this predates the lane; I did not re-run it. It is the alert path, not this lane.
problems.fix: Ticket for whoever owns the alert path.

budgets: Fresh npm run -s build, then perf_1080 --prod --no-build (counts are valid at any load; timing was not measured because the machine was busy, load 3.8-7.5): match peak 457k triangles (<= 500k), 260 draws (<= 450), 40 programs (<= 40), match memory peak renderer+GPU 1840 MB (<= 3000), Home 950 MB (<= 2500): GATE PASS. The audio lane does not touch the GPU. It adds about 17 MB of decoded audio at most, 1 ConvolverNode and about 2 GainNodes per spatial voice. npm run -s typecheck OK; npm run -s content:check 0 warnings; audio/build.py --gates PASS (kits, identity >= 8 dB, auto band, instant, impact laptop loss, as-heard, epic, wick gates); probe_audio_runtime match PASS x2 (lisvel seed 3, odrum seed 7); probe_audio_announcer, probe_audio_world and probe_audio_cc PASS. I restored _harness/_reports/perf_1080.json after the run.
notes: Pass: no broken item, no blocker, no budget miss, and no sensitivity or originality problem (every cue is VALE's own wax, tallow, brass, glass or bell material; nothing is gauge-derived). The lane is clearly better overall: the lane mix now belongs to the fighters, structures, states and zones have their own voices, the gold coin is crisp, and the maps have their own rooms. The score is held at 7.0, under the 7.5 par bar, because the core impact sound (SFX-2 transient and air, plus recipe-varied takes) is untouched, and that is where the mix still sits furthest from the gauge.
